key_insight: The nearly uniform upward liquid flow in clean spherical bubble chains is explained by the spatial distribution of overlapping far wakes from bubble trajectories, not by bubble dispersion width alone.
engineering_relevance: This provides a reduced-order way to predict bubble-induced liquid flow from measurable bubble paths, useful for designing and interpreting multiphase flow systems.
method: High-accuracy embedded-boundary simulations resolved interfacial boundary layers and long-range bubble interactions.
Hydrodynamic interactions were tracked in aligned bubble chains to identify when far-wake superposition is valid.
A reduced-order model based on isolated-bubble far wakes was applied to experimental bubble trajectories.
evidence_signal: The model reproduced the nearly uniform upward flow measured in experiments and showed that a uniformly dispersed arrangement instead yields a center-peaked velocity profile.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurately captured bubble trajectories and may be less reliable when bubble deformation, contamination, or strong near-field interactions invalidate far-wake superposition.
paper_title: Prediction of Spherical Bubble-Chain-Induced Liquid Flow through Far-Wake Superposition Based on Bubble-Chain Hydrodynamics
